answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of issuing it. Every new agent must post a bonded stake and pass an attested challenge requiring fresh inference plus a peer co-signature before it may transact. Ten thousand puppet agents thus cost ten thousand real computations and ten thousand locked bonds; one detected duplicate forfeits the bond, so a sybil swarm's cost scales linearly while its payoff stays flat. Honest agents earn a small nectar of fees for verifying attestations, the summit of the reputation ladder demands sustained service, and every slash lands on an auditable onyx ledger.
